# MCP tools

Everything the `anigram-mcp` server offers an assistant, with a real call against a built-in sheet and the start of its real answer. Install it with `claude mcp add anigram -- npx -y anigram-mcp` (more in [the MCP README](../../mcp/README.md)).

Most tools take a scene three ways: `id` for a built-in sheet, `file` for a scene file on disk, or `scene` for the JSON itself.

## Tools

- [`anigram_guide`](#anigram_guide): Scene format guide
- [`list_scenes`](#list_scenes): List built-in sheets
- [`get_scene`](#get_scene): Get a built-in sheet
- [`new_scene`](#new_scene): Start a new sheet
- [`validate_scene`](#validate_scene): Validate a scene
- [`write_scene`](#write_scene): Write a scene file
- [`edit_scene`](#edit_scene): Edit a scene
- [`simulate_scene`](#simulate_scene): Simulate a day
- [`check_scene`](#check_scene): Check a scene tells its story
- [`check_drawing`](#check_drawing): Check a sheet against its practice's rules
- [`lint_layout`](#lint_layout): Check the sheet reads cleanly
- [`auto_layout`](#auto_layout): Lay the sheet out by its flow
- [`export_dexpi`](#export_dexpi): Export a P&ID as DEXPI
- [`import_dexpi`](#import_dexpi): Open a DEXPI P&ID
- [`import_sfiles`](#import_sfiles): Open an SFILES 2.0 flowsheet
- [`export_sfiles`](#export_sfiles): Write a flowsheet as SFILES 2.0
- [`render_scene`](#render_scene): Draw the sheet
- [`share_link`](#share_link): Open it live

## anigram_guide

**Scene format guide** · read-only

Read this first. The scene file format: parts, behaviours, links, signal expressions, every part kind that has a drawing, and how to make a good sheet.

No parameters.

**Example**

```json
{}
```

```json

# The scene file

An Anigram drawing is one JSON file. It says **what the parts are, where they
sit and what flows between them** — never how anything animates. A flow
solver runs the network every tick and the sheet draws what it finds: line
width is flow, dot speed is flow, a turbine spins as fast as it generates.
So a scene can't show something its system isn't doing.

The five built-in sheets are scene files too (`list_scenes` / `get_scene` in
the MCP server, or `src/scenes/*.ts`). Read one before writing your own.

## Shape

```jsonc
{
  "anigram": 1,                    // the format version this file is written in
  "id": "narrowboat",              // lowercase-and-dashes
  "title": "A narrowboat",
  "subtitle": "Solar, a leisure battery and a diesel that charges it",
  "sheet": "LD-101",               // drawing number in the title block
  "size": [6, 4],                  // grid columns × rows; parts sit on cells
  "units": { "electric": { "rate": "kW", "amount": "kWh" } },
  "scale": { "electric": 2 },      // the flow that draws a link at full width
  "clock": { "start": 6, "rate": 0.6 },  // opening hour; simulated hours per second
  "knobs":    [{ "id": "cloud", "label": "cloud cover", "value": 0.3, "format": "{pct}%" }],
  "switches": [{ "id": "engine", "label": "engine running", "on": false }],
  "parts": [ … ],
  "links": [ … ],
  "captions": [{ "from": 6, "to": 10, "text": "Morning: the panels wake up…" }]
}
```

Only `id`, `title`, `size`, `parts` and `links` are required. `subtitle`
defaults to empty, `sheet` to `LD-100`, `clock` to `{ start: 6, rate: 1 }`.

`anigram` is the format version, currently `1`. Write it in every new file.
A file without it is read as version 1, and a file from an older version is
upgraded when it loads, so scene files and share links keep working as the
format grows. A file from a newer version than the reader knows is refused
... (523 more lines)
```

## new_scene

**Start a new sheet**

A small, working starter for a drawing practice: pictorial (the default), pid, single-line, pfd or fluid-power. It validates with no warnings and its `expect` list holds, and it shows the practice's conventions (tags, classes, instruments, title block). Edit it into the system you were asked for. With `file`, it is also saved there.

| parameter | type | required | what it is |
| - | - | - | - |
| `drawing` | string |  | the drawing practice; default pictorial One of `pictorial`, `pid`, `single-line`, `pfd`, `fluid-power`. |
| `id` | string |  | the new scene id, lowercase-and-dashes |
| `title` | string |  |  |
| `file` | string |  | save the starter to this .json path as well |

## validate_scene

**Validate a scene** · read-only

Check a scene file. Errors stop it loading; warnings are things that will run but probably are not what you meant (a part nothing feeds, two parts in one cell, a kind with no drawing).

| parameter | type | required | what it is |
| - | - | - | - |
| `scene` | object or string |  | a scene object (or its JSON text) |
| `file` | string |  | path to a .json scene file, relative to the working directory |

**Example**

```json
{
  "file": "my-plant.json"
}
```

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "errors": [],
  "warnings": []
}
```

## write_scene

**Write a scene file** · writes files

Validate a scene and save it as a .json file. Refuses to write a scene with errors unless `force` is set, so a file on disk always loads.

| parameter | type | required | what it is |
| - | - | - | - |
| `file` | string | yes | where to save it, a .json path relative to the working directory |
| `scene` | object or string | yes | the scene object (or its JSON text) |
| `force` | boolean |  | save even if it has errors |

**Example**

```json
{
  "file": "stub.json",
  "scene": {
    "anigram": 1,
    "id": "stub",
    "title": "Stub"
  },
  "force": true
}
```

```json
{
  "saved": "./stub.json",
  "ok": false,
  "errors": [
    "size: must be [columns, rows], whole numbers from 1 to 40",
    "parts: must be a non-empty array",
    "links: must be an array"
  ],
  "warnings": []
}
```

## edit_scene

**Edit a scene** · writes files

Apply small edits — add, move, update or remove parts and links, or set a top-level field — without rewriting the whole file. With `file`, the file is updated in place (only if the result is valid, unless `force`). Returns the edited scene and its validation.

| - | - | - | - |
| `scene` | object or string |  | a scene object (or its JSON text) |

| `id` | string |  | a built-in sheet id, e.g. "grid" — see list_scenes |

| `force` | boolean |  | save to `file` even if the result has errors |

## simulate_scene

**Simulate a day** · read-only

Run the scene headless through 24 hours from its opening hour and report what every part did, hour by hour, every alert (a demand going short, a store running empty, a link at its limit) and the day’s totals. Use it to check the drawing tells the story its captions claim, and to tune signals.

| parameter | type | required | what it is |
| - | - | - | - |
| `scene` | object or string |  | a scene object (or its JSON text) |
| `file` | string |  | path to a .json scene file, relative to the working directory |
| `id` | string |  | a built-in sheet id, e.g. "grid" — see list_scenes |
| `knobs` | object |  | slider values by knob id, e.g. { "cloud": 0.8 } |
| `switches` | object |  | switch states by id, e.g. { "mains": false } |
| `parts` | array |  | only show these part ids in the table |
| `format` | string |  | table (default) is a compact hour-by-hour text; json also puts every hourly number in the result One of `table`, `json`. |

**Example**

```json
{
  "id": "water-tower",
  "parts": [
    "tower",
    "pump"
  ]
}

## check_scene

**Check a scene tells its story** · read-only

One call for 'is it done?': validate the scene, run its day, and check every line of its `expect` list. ok is true only when the scene is valid and every expectation holds. Use it after each change; when one fails, the result says at which hours and what the parts it reads were doing. Warnings include physics: a machine made from nothing, a converter over 100% efficient, a round trip that comes back bigger. Fix those too, or the story only holds on paper. A scene with no `expect` list passes with a reminder to add one.

| parameter | type | required | what it is |
| - | - | - | - |
| `scene` | object or string |  | a scene object (or its JSON text) |
| `file` | string |  | path to a .json scene file, relative to the working directory |
| `id` | string |  | a built-in sheet id, e.g. "grid" — see list_scenes |
| `knobs` | object |  | slider values by knob id, e.g. { "cloud": 0.8 } |
| `switches` | object |  | switch states by id, e.g. { "mains": false } |

**Example**

```json
{
  "id": "water-tower"
}
```

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "errors": [],
  "warnings": [],
  "expect": [
    {
      "says": "at night the tower sits nearly full",
      "check": "part('tower').fill > 0.75",
      "ok": true,
      "hours": [
        4
      ],
      "failed": []
    },
    {
      "says": "morning showers drain it faster than the pump can refill it",
      "check": "part('tower').fill < 0.4 && part('pump').out > 0",
      "ok": true,
      "hours": [
        8
      ],
      "failed": []
    },
    {
      "says": "the pump rests once the tower is topped up",
      "check": "part('pump').out == 0",
      "ok": true,

        16
      ],

    },
    {

      "check": "part('taps').in >= 0.999 * part('taps').demand",

      "hours": [

## check_drawing

**Check a sheet against its practice's rules** · read-only

For an engineering drawing (pid, single-line, pfd, fluid-power): what an engineer reviewing the sheet would mark up. Every equipment item tagged in the practice's scheme (ISA letters on a P&ID, IEC 81346 on a single-line, ISO 1219-2 codes on a fluid-power circuit), lines and streams numbered, control valves driven by a controller and loops sharing a number, feeders and generators behind a breaker, oil returning to a tank, pumps behind a relief valve, air exhausting through a silencer, the title block filled. Each finding names its rule and says how to fix it. Advisory by default: ok stays true. With `strict` (for CI and print-ready sheets), ok is false while any finding is left. A pictorial sheet has no practice rules and passes.

| parameter | type | required | what it is |
| - | - | - | - |
| `scene` | object or string |  | a scene object (or its JSON text) |
| `file` | string |  | path to a .json scene file, relative to the working directory |
| `id` | string |  | a built-in sheet id, e.g. "grid" — see list_scenes |
| `strict` | boolean |  | make every finding a failure; default false |

**Example**

```json
{
  "file": "my-plant.json"
}
```

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "drawing": "pid",
  "strict": false,
  "errors": [],
  "findings": []
}
```

## lint_layout

**Check the sheet reads cleanly** · read-only

Check the drawing's geometry without rendering it: lines that cross or run on top of each other, a line through a part that is not one of its ends, slanted runs, labels landing on parts or other labels, and labels running off the edge of the sheet. Each finding says what to move. Engineering sheets are checked as they draw (only the lines the practice shows, busbars tapped where their feeders are). auto_layout fixes most of these at once.

| parameter | type | required | what it is |
| - | - | - | - |
| `scene` | object or string |  | a scene object (or its JSON text) |
| `file` | string |  | path to a .json scene file, relative to the working directory |
| `id` | string |  | a built-in sheet id, e.g. "grid" — see list_scenes |

**Example**

```json
{
  "id": "grid"
}
```

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "errors": [],
  "findings": []
}
```

## auto_layout

**Lay the sheet out by its flow**

Place every part on the grid by how things flow, as a drafter would: sources first, each step one column on, lines straight where they can be and turning square where they cannot, long links routed through empty cells, and P&ID instruments a row above what they serve. Single-line diagrams run top to bottom (supply at the top, feeders dropping off the busbars, loads at the bottom); fluid-power circuits bottom to top (pump and tank at the bottom, actuators at the top); everything else runs left to right, or set `direction`. It rewrites `at`, `via`, `bend`, `labelSide`, instrument cells and `size`, and nothing else. With `file`, the file is updated in place. Returns the scene and a lint_layout of the result; nudge anything it leaves with edit_scene.

| parameter | type | required | what it is |
| - | - | - | - |
| `scene` | object or string |  | a scene object (or its JSON text) |
| `file` | string |  | path to a .json scene file, relative to the working directory |
| `id` | string |  | a built-in sheet id, e.g. "grid" — see list_scenes |
| `direction` | string |  | which way the flow runs; default down for a single-line, up for a fluid-power circuit, right otherwise One of `right`, `down`, `up`. |

**Example**

```json
{
  "id": "water-tower",
  "direction": "right"
}
```

```json
{
  "direction": "right",
  "moved": [
    "mains",
    "pump",
    "works",
    "tower",
    "main",
    "taps",
    "valve",
    "hydrant"
  ],
  "scene": {
    "anigram": 1,
    "id": "water-tower",
    "title": "A town’s water",
    "subtitle": "Why towns keep a tank on stilts: a pump that can’t keep up with breakfast, and gravity that can",

    "size": [
      7,

      }
    },
    "scale": {

    },
    "clock": {

## export_dexpi

**Export a P&ID as DEXPI**

Write a P&ID (`"drawing": "pid"`) as DEXPI 1.3 Proteus XML, the exchange format plant design software reads: equipment with its tags and nozzles, each numbered line as a piping system with its valves in place, off-page connectors, and the instrument loops (measuring, control, actuated valves). It carries the plant, not the picture: positions are in millimetres on A3, and the receiving tool draws its own symbols. With `out` (a .xml path) the file is saved and only a summary comes back. notes say what could not go across (a part with no DEXPI class, a valve outside any pipe); run check_drawing first so every item is tagged and every line numbered.

| parameter | type | required | what it is |
| - | - | - | - |
| `scene` | object or string |  | a scene object (or its JSON text) |
| `file` | string |  | path to a .json scene file, relative to the working directory |
| `id` | string |  | a built-in sheet id, e.g. "grid" — see list_scenes |
| `out` | string |  | save the XML to this .xml path |

**Example**

```json
{
  "file": "my-plant.json"
}
```

```json
{
  "counts": {
    "equipment": 2,
    "lines": 4,
    "segments": 4,
    "instruments": 2,
    "loops": 1
  },
  "notes": [],
  "bytes": 25403
}
```

## import_dexpi

**Open a DEXPI P&ID**

Turn a DEXPI 1.3 (Proteus XML) P&ID from plant design software into a living P&ID scene: equipment with its tags, each piping segment as lines from nozzle to nozzle with its valves in place, off-page connectors as where flow enters and leaves, and the instrument loops with the valves they drive. Flanges and reducers are passed through. Behaviours are guessed from each class (a pump passes up to its duty and can be stopped, a hand valve can be shut, a control valve follows a slider, a tank stores) and the notes say so: set real duties, then add an `expect` list and run check_scene. Give `file` (a .xml path) or the XML itself; with `out` (a .json path) the scene is saved and not echoed back.

| parameter | type | required | what it is |
| - | - | - | - |
| `file` | string |  | path to a DEXPI .xml file |
| `xml` | string |  | the DEXPI XML itself |
| `layout` | string |  | `drawing` keeps the file's own arrangement, `flow` lays it out by its flow; by default whichever reads more cleanly One of `drawing`, `flow`. |
| `sceneId` | string |  | the new scene's id |
| `out` | string |  | save the scene to this .json path |

**Example**

```json
{
  "file": "reference-pid.xml",
  "out": "reference-pid.json"
}
```

```json
{
  "counts": {
    "equipment": 5,
    "valves": 11,
    "lines": 11,
    "instruments": 4,
    "fittings": 3
  },
  "notes": [
    "2 exchangers: the utility side (a line from off the sheet, through it and off again) is drawn as heat taken from the process, a tenth of the flow it pas...
    "behaviours are guessed from each class (supplies of 90 m³/h in, demands of 60 m³/h out, pumps rated 90 m³/h): set real duties and demands before trustin...
    "laid out by its flow, which reads more cleanly here than the file's own arrangement (1 layout findings against 3); pass layout \"drawing\" to keep the f...
  ],
  "saved": "./reference-pid.json"
}
```

## import_sfiles

**Open an SFILES 2.0 flowsheet**

Turn an SFILES 2.0 string, the line notation for flowsheets, into a living process flow diagram laid out by its flow: `(raw)(pp)(hex)(r)[(prod)](dist){tout}(prod)`. Units are `(raw)` feed, `(prod)` product, `(pp)` pump, `(comp)` compressor, `(hex)` heat exchanger, `(r)` reactor, `(dist)` column, `(flash)` flash drum, `(tank)`, `(v)` valve, `(mix)`/`(splt)`, `(lfil)` filter and the rest of the OntoCape set; `[...]` branches, `<&|...&|` flows in, digits and `<digit` are recycles. Major equipment gets tags (P-101, E-101, C-101), behaviours are guessed as for a DEXPI import, and control units are left out. With `out` (a .json path) the scene is saved and not echoed back.

| parameter | type | required | what it is |
| - | - | - | - |
| `sfiles` | string | yes | the SFILES 2.0 string |
| `title` | string |  | the sheet's title |
| `sceneId` | string |  | the new scene's id |
| `drawing` | string |  | pfd (the default), or pid to draw the valves too One of `pfd`, `pid`. |
| `out` | string |  | save the scene to this .json path |

**Example**

```json
{
  "sfiles": "(raw)(mix)<1(pp)(hex)(r)(dist)[{bout}(prod)]{tout}(splt)1(prod)",
  "title": "Reactor with recycle",
  "out": "reactor.json"
}
```

```json
{
  "counts": {
    "units": 9,
    "streams": 9,
    "recycles": 1,
    "controls": 0
  },
  "notes": [
    "outlet tags ({tout}, {bout}, {hot_in}…) are read but not drawn: each stream is one line",
    "behaviours are guessed from each unit (feeds of 90 m³/h, products sharing 60 m³/h for each feed, pumps rated 90 m³/h): set real duties before trusting a...
    "flow is pulled by what the products take, so a recycle only carries what the feeds cannot supply: it is drawn, but idle while they keep up"
  ],
  "saved": "./reactor.json"
}
```

## export_sfiles

**Write a flowsheet as SFILES 2.0**

Write a scene's process streams (water, heat and fuel; not power, signals or losses) as an SFILES 2.0 string, the line notation flowsheet tools and machine-learning datasets read. Each part becomes a unit by its class, then its label (a "Reactor", a "Flash drum"), then its role: sources are `(raw)`, sinks `(prod)`. Branches, recycles and feeds joining the main line are written the way the notation does.

| parameter | type | required | what it is |
| - | - | - | - |
| `scene` | object or string |  | a scene object (or its JSON text) |
| `file` | string |  | path to a .json scene file, relative to the working directory |
| `id` | string |  | a built-in sheet id, e.g. "grid" — see list_scenes |

**Example**

```json
{
  "file": "reactor.json"
}
```

```json
{
  "sfiles": "(raw)(mix)<1(pp)(hex)(r)(dist)[(prod)](splt)1(prod)",
  "notes": []
}
```

## render_scene

**Draw the sheet**

Draw the sheet at an hour of the day, the same drawing the app shows in paper mode: every flow labelled with its value and direction. The scene runs from its opening hour first, so tanks and batteries show real levels. By default it comes back as a PNG image: look at it to check the layout (crossed lines, labels on top of each other, parts too close) and fix the scene. format svg returns the markup instead. With `out`, the drawing is saved to that .png, .svg or .pdf path and only its details are returned. A PDF is one landscape page of ISO A paper (A3 unless `paper` says otherwise) for printing and filing; an engineering drawing carries its title block. A PDF needs `out`.

| parameter | type | required | what it is |
| - | - | - | - |
| `scene` | object or string |  | a scene object (or its JSON text) |
| `file` | string |  | path to a .json scene file, relative to the working directory |
| `id` | string |  | a built-in sheet id, e.g. "grid" — see list_scenes |
| `knobs` | object |  | slider values by knob id, e.g. { "cloud": 0.8 } |
| `switches` | object |  | switch states by id, e.g. { "mains": false } |
| `hour` | number |  | hour of day to draw, e.g. 18.5; default the opening hour |
| `theme` | string |  |  One of `light`, `dark`. |
| `labels` | boolean |  | label every flow (default true) |
| `credit` | boolean |  | sign the bottom corner "Made with Anigram · Vaibhav Patel" (default true; false leaves it off) |
| `format` | string |  | png (default) to look at; svg for the markup; pdf to print. With `out`, taken from its extension One of `png`, `svg`, `pdf`. |
| `paper` | string |  | the PDF page, landscape; default A3 One of `A4`, `A3`, `A2`, `A1`. |
| `width` | integer |  | PNG width in pixels, default 1600 |
| `out` | string |  | save to this .png, .svg or .pdf path instead of returning it |

**Example**

```json
{
  "id": "water-tower",
  "hour": 7,
  "format": "svg"
}
```

```json
{
  "hour": 7,
  "format": "svg",
  "bytes": 14319,
  "aspect": 1.513
}
```

## share_link

**Open it live** · read-only

A link that opens the scene running live in the Anigram app — the whole scene travels in the URL, so nothing is uploaded. view: app (the workbench, default), embed (just the sheet, for an iframe), paper (frozen and labelled), screen (full-bleed wall view).

| parameter | type | required | what it is |
| - | - | - | - |
| `scene` | object or string |  | a scene object (or its JSON text) |
| `file` | string |  | path to a .json scene file, relative to the working directory |
| `id` | string |  | a built-in sheet id, e.g. "grid" — see list_scenes |
| `view` | string |  |  One of `app`, `embed`, `paper`, `screen`, `editor`. |
| `hour` | number |  |  |
| `theme` | string |  |  One of `light`, `dark`. |

**Example**

```json
{
  "id": "water-tower",
  "hour": 7
}
```

```json
{
  "url": "https://anigram.vaibhav.co.uk/?t=7&scene=water-tower",
  "length": 52
}
```

## Prompts

Ready-made instructions an assistant can start from, one per drawing practice.

| prompt | what it's for |
| - | - |
| `draw-sheet` | Draw a pictorial sheet of a system with Anigram. |
| `draw-pid` | Draw a P&ID of a system with Anigram, following ISO 10628-2 symbols, ISA-5.1 tags and lines. |
| `draw-single-line` | Draw a single-line diagram of a system with Anigram, following IEC 60617 (or ANSI/IEEE 315) symbols, IEC 81346 tags. |
| `draw-pfd` | Draw a process flow diagram of a system with Anigram, following ISO 10628-1 major equipment and streams. |
| `draw-fluid-power` | Draw a fluid-power circuit diagram of a system with Anigram, following ISO 1219-1 symbols, laid out and tagged after ISO 1219-2. |
